observation.visible_scene: A static, eye-level view of a fog-shrouded mountain slope. In the lower-left foreground a large grey boulder holds a person's foot in a maroon sneaker with a white sole, mostly motionless. A thin pinkish grass stalk with forked seed heads rises in the left foreground, slightly out of focus. The mid-ground is a steep ridge densely covered with dark green conifers, their upper portions dissolving into white mist. On the right stands a mostly bare, gnarled tree with a few green leaves on its lower branches, set against a uniformly white foggy sky. The overall lighting is flat and overcast.
visible_changes: The foreground grass stalk sways gently: its top and forked seed heads shift left-right and tilt slightly between frames, while its base stays fixed on the rock, indicating wind motion rather than camera motion.

The fog over the ridge thickens/encroaches gradually: the treetops at the crest of the forested hill, fairly distinct early in the clip, become progressively more washed out and obscured by mist toward the later frames, lowering the visible tree line.

The bare tree on the right, the boulder, the sneaker, and the lower vegetation remain essentially stationary; no camera pan or zoom is evident because these fixed elements keep the same framing throughout.
No object enters, exits, or completes an action within the segment; the changes are limited to subtle sway and slow fog drift.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the fog movement (wind direction, temperature) and whether the mist will continue to thicken or clear after the clip ends.
The person's body and posture beyond the single visible foot/shoe.
Whether the grass stalk was already swaying before t=0 and continues after t=2.67.
uncertain_details: The fog change could be either a real thickening of mist over the ridge or a slow horizontal drift of a fog bank; the frames do not clearly distinguish the two.
The exact amount of grass-stalk sway is small and partly ambiguous against the soft focus.
Camera is treated as static, but very slight handheld jitter cannot be fully ruled out given the uniform foggy background.
